scholarships.title: MIT Undergraduate Need-Based Financial Aid and MIT Scholarship for International Students
scholarships.funding_label: Need-based grant aid (MIT meets 100% of demonstrated need)

eligibility: Classified as an international student for financial aid purposes (not eligible for U.S. federal student financial aid per FAFSA eligibility rules)
Applies for undergraduate admission to MIT
Submits the CSS Profile designating MIT (CSS Code 3514)
Submits parental tax returns or income documentation for both parents via IDOC
Demonstrates financial need; there are no fee waivers for international students on the CSS Profile
existing.eligibility_summary: Any applicant classified as international for federal financial aid purposes (not eligible for FAFSA-based federal aid) who applies for admission to MIT as an undergraduate and submits the CSS Profile plus parental income documentation. Awarding is based solely on demonstrated financial need.
benefits: Tuition and fees up to 100% of MIT's calculated demonstrated need
Health Insurance Grant covering the MIT Student Health Insurance Plan for highest-need undergraduates who lack adequate coverage
First Year Grant of $2,000 for highest-need first-year students, split equally between fall and spring
coverage: Tuition and fees up to 100% of MIT's calculated demonstrated need
Health Insurance Grant covering the MIT Student Health Insurance Plan for highest-need undergraduates who lack adequate coverage
First Year Grant of $2,000 for highest-need first-year students, split equally between fall and spring
requirements: Submit the CSS Profile and all MIT supplemental CSS questions
Upload parent income documents to the College Board IDOC platform, not directly to MIT
Allow up to two weeks for IDOC delivery of tax returns to MIT
Allow about 10 business days for documents to appear in the MIT Online Financial Aid System
documents: CSS Profile (College Board) designating MIT, CSS Code 3514
Parents' income tax returns or wage statements from two years ago
Parents' tax return from their country of residence plus an English translation if parents live outside the U.S.
Records of untaxed income, current bank account balances and records of investments
application_method: Submit the CSS Profile online through the College Board
Submit parental tax returns or income documentation to the College Board's Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC)
Track documents and view the aid offer in the MIT Application Portal
existing.selection_notes: Awards are made on the basis of financial need alone; about 58% of MIT undergraduates receive an MIT Scholarship.
existing.best_fit: International undergraduates admitted to MIT whose families cannot fund the MIT cost of attendance and who are willing to document family income in detail through the CSS Profile process.
existing.notes: The award is a grant, not a loan. Awarded students must complete a Student Information Review Form between May 1 and July 1 each year so MIT can match them to the correct endowed scholarship fund.
existing.duration: Aid is awarded for each academic year of the undergraduate degree and reviewed annually; continuing students reapply by February 15.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle. Early Action November 30, Regular Action February 15, Transfer February 15; aid documents manageable through the MIT Application Portal until mid-May.
existing.deadline_display: To apply for financial aid, all students must submit the CSS Profile and parental tax returns or income documentation through IDOC by the following deadlines: Early Action November 30, Regular Action February 15, Transfer February 15. MIT publishes no calendar year for these dates.
existing.program_type: Need-blind institutional need-based grant aid for undergraduate international students at a private research university.
